Hi Sarah — quick, concrete answers followed by examples. I'll keep the technicalities minimal and provide numeric scenarios you can paste into a spreadsheet.

Short answers:
- System messages: counted as input tokens. Anything sent in the request payload that consumes model context (system/user/assistant messages and tool prompts) is billed as input tokens.
- Tool outputs: billed as generated/output tokens. When a request invokes multiple tools, the tokens produced by each tool call are included in the request's generated token total. On monthly invoices we also provide an itemized breakdown that attributes generated tokens to the tool call that produced them (if applicable).
- Streaming and cancellation: billing is based on completed tokens. If you cancel mid-stream, only fully emitted tokens are billed. Partial bytes inside an incomplete tokenizer unit are buffered and only counted when the tokenizer completes a token. Practically, streaming does not cause double-billing — you pay for the tokens the model actually produced before cancellation.
- Rounding: token counts are integer token units for billing. For a single API request we round up fractional tokenizer counts to the next whole token (this is rare because the tokenizer emits whole tokens). Monthly aggregation is the exact sum of per-request billed tokens; we do not re-round aggregates to a different scheme later.
- Prefix/KV cache: when a cached prefix is reused we avoid sending identical context to the model; billed input reflects the actual context the model evaluated. In other words, cache hits reduce billed input tokens to the number of tokens the model actually processed for that call.

Numeric examples (simple, paste-friendly):
Example A — single request with system + user prompt, one generated response
- System prompt: 25 tokens
- User prompt: 110 tokens
- Model generated: 210 tokens
Billing: input = 135 tokens (system + user), output = 210 tokens. Total billed tokens = 345.

Example B — two tool calls then model final generation
- System prompt: 20 tokens
- User prompt: 80 tokens
- Tool A call: tool prompt -> model fetch (tool output 90 tokens)
- Tool B call: tool prompt -> tool output 30 tokens
- Model final response (uses tool outputs): 160 tokens
Billing: input = 100 tokens (system + user); generated = 90 + 30 + 160 = 280 tokens. Total billed tokens = 380. Invoice itemization will show generated tokens split across Tool A (90), Tool B (30), Model generation (160).

Example C — streaming & cancellation
- System + user total input: 60 tokens
- Model begins streaming and emits 120 tokens, you cancel after the 80th token completes
Billing: input = 60 tokens; output = 80 tokens (only the fully emitted tokens). Total billed tokens = 140.

Edge notes:
- We count tokens after tokenization (BPE/byte-pair units); there are no per-byte charges.
- If you rely heavily on prefix caching (same >90% prefix reuse), your effective per-request billed input can be much lower than the raw prompt size because only the delta is sent to the model.
- Our invoice format supports line items for: hosted-model generation, tool-generated tokens, embeddings, and any per-call add-ons.

If you want, I can convert the above examples into a CSV showing per-request lines for your FP&A model.
